qualitative.filing_summary_10k: NIKE's fiscal 2026 10-K reports total revenues of $46.4 billion, roughly flat versus fiscal 2025, with gross margin up 20 basis points to 42.9% but net income down 3% to $3.1 billion. Wholesale revenue grew while NIKE Direct (stores and digital) revenue declined on lower traffic; Greater China and Converse revenues fell notably amid ongoing brand and marketplace repositioning efforts the company expects to substantially complete by December 2026. The filing also discusses $385 million in severance charges and a $986 million benefit recognized from anticipated recovery of previously paid IEEPA tariffs following a Supreme Court ruling.
qualitative.filing_summary_10q: The excerpt provided for the most recent 10-Q (for the quarter ended February 28, 2026, fiscal 2026 Q3) consists only of XBRL data tags and cover-page identifiers rather than narrative financial disclosure, so specific reported figures or discussion of the quarter's results cannot be summarized from what was given.
qualitative.filing_summary_8k: This 8-K, dated September 15-16, 2026, discloses that NIKE's Board of Directors expanded to twelve members and appointed Alexandre Arnault, Deputy CEO of Moët Hennessy (LVMH), as a new director effective immediately, with a term through the 2027 annual meeting; he received a $200,000 sign-on restricted stock grant under the standard director compensation program. The filing also notes a press release announcing the appointment was furnished under Item 7.01 (Regulation FD Disclosure).
qualitative.moat_explanation: The 10-K describes NIKE as 'the largest seller of athletic footwear and apparel in the world' and details substantial ongoing investment in demand creation (brand marketing and sports marketing expense of ~$4.75 billion in fiscal 2026) as well as a portfolio of owned brands (NIKE, Jordan, Converse) and licensing revenue, consistent with a brand-based intangible asset moat rather than a cost, network, or switching-cost advantage described in the excerpts.
red_flags: Greater China revenues declined 11% (13% currency-neutral) amid 'declining store traffic, elevated promotional activity and higher levels of inventory across the marketplace,' with negative impacts expected to continue through fiscal 2027
Converse revenues fell 31% and EBIT fell 93% as the brand undergoes a 'strategic reset'
NIKE Direct digital sales declined 12% (currency-neutral), attributed to reduced traffic, and overall NIKE Direct revenue fell 6%
Company recognized $385 million in employee severance charges in fiscal 2026 and states it 'may take additional actions which could lead to additional charges in future quarters'
Effective tax rate rose from 17.1% to 20.3%, partly due to non-recurrence of a prior-year one-time tax benefit

Exposure to tariff policy volatility, illustrated by a $986 million IEEPA tariff benefit recognized in fiscal 2026 tied to a Supreme Court ruling, with continued monitoring of tariff/litigation developments
